question: What do 2.5 mg and 5 mg of mixed amphetamine salts do in adults without ADHD?

sources.title: Neurocognitive, Autonomic, and Mood Effects of Adderall: A Pilot Study of Healthy College Students

findings.finding: Small, mixed cognitive effects; large autonomic, subjective and activated-emotion effects.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: Adderall had minimal, but mixed, effects on cognitive processes relevant to neurocognitive enhancement (small effects), and substantial effects on autonomic responses, subjective drug experiences, and positive states of activated emotion (large effects).

sources.title: Not so smart? "Smart" drugs increase the level but decrease the quality of cognitive effort

findings.finding: On knapsack optimization, all three drugs raised effort and lowered solution value; productivity fell.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: Effort (decision time and number of steps taken to find a solution) increases significantly, but productivity (quality of effort) decreases significantly.

sources.title: Prescription Stimulants' Effects on Healthy Inhibitory Control, Working Memory, and Episodic Memory: A Meta-analysis

findings.finding: Small effects of prescription stimulants on inhibitory control and delayed episodic memory in healthy adults; working-memory effects small and inconsistent.

sources.title: Effect of d-amphetamine on post-error slowing in healthy volunteers

findings.finding: 5 mg had no significant effect on any outcome; only 20 mg changed behavior.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: Amphetamine (20 mg) reduced post-error slowing, consistent with a dampened behavioral reactivity to errors.

sources.title: Are attention lapses related to d-amphetamine liking?

findings.finding: 5 mg produced near-zero 'feel drug' ratings (adjusted mean 0.10).
findings.exactSourceLanguage: neither the 5- nor 10-mg dose produced appreciable levels of liking or euphoria

sources.title: Subjective responses predict d-amphetamine choice in healthy volunteers

findings.finding: 81 of 112 chose amphetamine over placebo; choosers had greater positive mood, elation and systolic blood pressure rise.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: Eighty-one participants chose amphetamine (Choosers) while 31 chose placebo (Non-choosers).

exposures.dose: 20 mg as four 5 mg capsules; choice of 1–4

sources.title: Systematic reviews of the acute effects of amphetamine on working memory and other cognitive performances in healthy individuals, with a focus on the potential influence of personality traits

findings.finding: Tabulates a 5 mg d-amphetamine study (Schmedtje 1988) with no main effect on digit span, digit-symbol substitution, memory or simple reaction time.
Personality traits shape the subjective effects of amphetamine; few studies report their effect on objective performance.

sources.title: Effect of a Single Oral Dose of Dexamphetamine or Zolpidem on Attention and Reaction Time in Healthy Men

findings.finding: Modest effects at 3 h; fewer sustained-attention omissions at 8 h; no relation between plasma concentration and performance.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: No correlation between drug plasma concentration and cognitive performance measures was demonstrable

sources.title: Human response to repeated low-dose d-amphetamine: evidence for behavioral enhancement and tolerance
sources.journal: Neuropsychopharmacology : official publication of the American College of Neuropsychopharmacology

findings.finding: Vigor and euphoria peaked after the third dose; liking peaked at the first; effects greater in women.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: Subjective ratings of vigor and euphoria exhibited the greatest response following the third dose of the AAA group, as hypothesized. In contrast, drug liking was greatest following a single or first d-amphetamine dose. These effects were greater in women.

sources.title: How effective are pharmaceuticals for cognitive enhancement in healthy adults? A series of meta-analyses of cognitive performance during acute administration of modafinil, methylphenidate and D-amphetamine
sources.journal: European neuropsychopharmacology : the journal of the European College of Neuropsychopharmacology

findings.finding: 47 studies; small overall effects for modafinil and methylphenidate; none for d-amphetamine.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: There were no effects for d-amph.

sources.title: Risk of Incident Psychosis and Mania With Prescription Amphetamines

findings.finding: Past-month prescription amphetamine: adjusted OR 2.68 for incident psychosis or mania; >30 mg dextroamphetamine-equivalent: 5.28-fold.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: high doses of amphetamines (>30 mg dextroamphetamine equivalents) were associated with 5.28-fold increased odds of psychosis or mania

sources.title: Psychosis with Methylphenidate or Amphetamine in Patients with ADHD
sources.journal: The New England journal of medicine

findings.finding: New-onset psychosis in 0.21% on amphetamine vs 0.10% on methylphenidate; HR 1.65.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: new-onset psychosis occurred in approximately 1 in 660 patients. Amphetamine use was associated with a greater risk of psychosis than methylphenidate.

sources.population: ages 13–25 with ADHD starting a stimulant

sources.title: Objective and subjective cognitive enhancing effects of mixed amphetamine salts in healthy people

findings.finding: No enhancement of any of 13 cognitive measures for participants in general; participants believed they were enhanced.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: participants nevertheless believed their performance was more enhanced by the active capsule than by placebo

sources.title: Effects of d-amphetamine on task performance and social behavior of humans in a residential laboratory

findings.finding: Faster responding without accuracy change; no change in self-reported drug effects.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: d-Amphetamine increased response rate without affecting accuracy on some tasks.

sources.title: The effects of repeated amphetamine exposure on multiple measures of human behavior

findings.finding: Behavioral effects (food intake, task accuracy, talking, smoking) showed no tolerance; subjective ratings showed rapid tolerance.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: No tolerance to these effects was observed. Increases in VAS ratings of dose "potency" and "liking," as well as "stimulated" and "anxious," and decreases in "sedated" were observed during initial amphetamine exposure, but tolerance to these effects developed rapidly.

sources.title: Low-dose amphetamine salts and adult attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder

findings.finding: 54% responded; mean responder end dose 10.77 mg/day.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: The mean end dose for responders was 10.77 mg/day (0.14 mg/kg/day).

sources.title: Acute effects of lisdexamfetamine and D-amphetamine on social cognition and cognitive performance in a placebo-controlled study in healthy subjects

findings.finding: Improved go-accuracy and vigilance; no digit-span effect.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: D-Amphetamine and lisdexamfetamine increased cognitive performance (go-accuracy and vigilance on the SST and MCT, respectively).

sources.title: The effects of dexamphetamine on simulated driving performance

findings.finding: Worse daytime simulated driving; incorrect signalling, red-light failures, slow reactions.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: "incorrect signalling", "failing to stop at a red traffic light" and "slow reaction times" were the behaviours most strongly affected by dexamphetamine

sources.title: Inattention, impulsive action, and subjective response to D-amphetamine

findings.finding: Attention lapses predict less, impulsive action more, subjective response; associations strengthen with dose.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: a dose-response relationship was observed, such that the strength of these associations increased with higher doses of amphetamine

sources.title: To choose or not to choose: Examining the influence of choice on elicitation of subjective and objective prescription stimulant placebo effects in the laboratory

findings.finding: Believing one took Adderall produced medium-large subjective effects and no objective cognitive effects.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: These results provide further evidence of medium-large placebo effects for subjective, but not objective, outcomes following expected prescription stimulant use.

sources.title: Effect of amphetamines on blood pressure
sources.journal: The Cochrane database of systematic reviews

findings.finding: Daily oral amphetamines raise SBP 1.93 mmHg, DBP 1.84 mmHg, heart rate 3.71 bpm, sustained at ≥8 weeks.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: amphetamines increased systolic blood pressure (SBP) by 1.93 mmHg (95% CI 1.54 to 2.31) and diastolic blood pressure (DBP) by 1.84 mmHg (95% CI 1.51 to 2.16)

sources.population: 56 RCTs, adults and children; North America, Europe, Japan, Australia

sources.title: The Impact of Dexamphetamine Treatment for Obesity on Executive Function: A Double-Blind Randomised Controlled Pilot Study

findings.finding: Six weeks of dexamphetamine had no effect on executive function versus placebo.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: There was no discernible impact of amphetamine treatment for obesity on executive function.

sources.title: Catecholamine influences on dorsolateral prefrontal cortical networks

findings.finding: Prefrontal function follows an inverted U in catecholamine level.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: The dorsolateral PFC is especially sensitive to levels of norepinephrine and dopamine, whereby either too little or too much markedly impairs PFC function.

sources.title: ADDERALL (dextroamphetamine saccharate, amphetamine aspartate, dextroamphetamine sulfate and amphetamine sulfate tablets)

findings.finding: Each tablet is equal parts four salts; IR peak about 3 h; 10 mg d-amphetamine solution gives peak ≈ 33.2 ng/mL and half-life ≈ 11.75 h in healthy volunteers.
